# Tidepool Landing Page: Build Plan

**Visual direction:** Tidepool is about small teams tracking a shared week, so the palette shifts from forest-and-coral to tide-pool tones: deep teal-navy (#0F3B45) for backgrounds, sand (#F3EADB) for light sections, seafoam (#7FC8B8) for highlights, and coral (#F26B5B) reserved for CTAs and the single hand-drawn annotation. Headlines use a warm geometric sans; body uses a neutral sans at 18px minimum.

**1. Navigation.** Slim bar on teal. Logo left, three links (Product, Teams, Pricing), a coral "Start a week" button right. Sticky on scroll.

**2. Hero.** Two columns. Left: headline, 14-word subhead, and CTA with a secondary "See a sample week" text link. Right: a screenshot of a team's week board, slightly tilted. A hand-drawn coral arrow runs from the headline to the screenshot's Tuesday column. Headline copy: "Your team's week, planned together." Subhead: "Tidepool gives small teams one shared week: who's doing what, when, and what's still open."

**3. Week timeline (signature element).** Full-width sand band. A vertical Monday–Sunday rail runs down the left side as a sticky sidebar. Each day is a node showing that day's commitments as small avatar chips. Scrolling highlights the active day. Copy: "Seven days, one view. Nothing lives in someone's head."

**4. Problem.** Centered, teal background, three short lines of stacked text: "Plans in group chat. Tasks in a spreadsheet. Deadlines in someone's inbox." Then a turn: "Tidepool puts them on one page."

**5. Core features.** Three cards, each with a single line illustration in seafoam: Shared week (live sync), Handoffs (assign and nudge), Weekly review (a closing summary every Friday). Plain verb-led titles, two-sentence descriptions.

**6. Pull quote.** Full-width, sand background. Customer quote set in monospace at large size, attributed with role and team size ("Ops lead, 6-person agency"). Coral quotation mark only.

**7. Proof.** Row of six anonymized team-type labels ("Remote design studio, 5 people") rather than logos, since small teams often lack recognizable brands.

**8. How it works.** Three numbered steps with a small screenshot each: create the week, add your people, close the week on Friday. Monospace step labels.

**9. Pricing.** Two tiers, free for teams up to four, flat monthly for larger. Copy avoids jargon.

**10. Final CTA.** Teal band, one line: "Start next Monday with a plan everyone can see." Coral button, no competing links.

**11. Footer.** Minimal links, privacy and status, small tide-line illustration.

# Tidepool Landing Page: Revised Build Plan

**What changed:** The first draft borrowed the reference's devices without a reason tied to Tidepool. This version keeps the signature moves only where they explain the product: the week rail shows the week, the arrow leads to the proof, and the monospace quote marks a real person's words. It also fixes the subhead (it ran 15 words, not 14), adds a mobile treatment, and replaces invented-sounding copy with sourcing rules.

**Visual system:** Deep teal-navy (#0F3B45) for dark sections, sand (#F3EADB) for light sections, seafoam (#7FC8B8) for illustration and highlights, coral (#F26B5B) only for buttons and the single hand-drawn arrow. Headlines in a warm geometric sans; body in a neutral sans at 18px minimum, 4.5:1 contrast or better. Monospace appears only in the pull quote and step labels. Motion is limited to the timeline's active-day highlight and a short fade on scroll, with reduced-motion respected.

**1. Navigation.** Slim teal bar. Logo left; Product, Teams, Pricing center; "Start a week" coral button right. Sticky, with a thin seafoam underline on the active link.

**2. Hero.** Two columns on desktop, stacked on mobile. Left: headline "Your team's week, planned together." Subhead (14 words): "Tidepool gives small teams one shared week: who does what, when, and what's still open." Primary CTA "Start a week," secondary text link "See a sample week." Right: a slightly tilted screenshot of a real-looking team board. A hand-drawn coral arrow runs from the headline to the Tuesday column, the one place the eye should land next.

**3. Week rail (signature section).** Sand band. On desktop, a sticky vertical Monday–Sunday rail on the left; each day is a node with avatar chips for that day's commitments. Scrolling activates the matching node. On mobile, the rail becomes a horizontal day strip pinned at the top of the section. Copy: "Seven days, one view. Nothing lives in someone's head."

**4. Problem.** Teal background, centered. Three short fragments in stacked type: "Plans in the group chat. Tasks in a spreadsheet. Deadlines in someone's inbox." Then the turn, in seafoam: "Tidepool puts them on one page."

**5. Features.** Three cards on sand, each with a single seafoam line illustration: Shared week, Handoffs, Friday review. Verb-led titles, two-sentence descriptions. Each card links to its product section.

**6. Pull quote.** Full-width, teal background. Quote in monospace at large size, coral quotation mark only. Attribution gives role and team size ("Ops lead, 6-person agency"). Rule: use only real customer words with written permission. If none exist at launch, hold this section and use the Friday summary screenshot as a stand-in.

**7. Proof.** Six anonymized team-type labels in a row ("Remote design studio, 5 people") with a small count of active weeks, if the number is real. No logos or invented metrics.

**8. How it works.** Three numbered steps on sand, each with a small screenshot: create the week, add your people, close the week Friday. Monospace step labels. Each step ends in a one-line outcome, not a feature name.

**9. Pricing.** Two tiers on sand: free for teams up to four, flat monthly for larger teams with the price shown as a placeholder until finalized. Plain language, no "seats" or "workspaces."

**10. Final CTA.** Full-width teal band. One line: "Start next Monday with a plan everyone can see." Single coral button, no competing links.

**11. Footer.** Teal, minimal. Product, privacy, status, and contact links. A small tide-line illustration in seafoam.

**Before launch:** check the arrow still points correctly at mobile widths, confirm all quotes and counts are real, and run an accessibility pass on the rail's keyboard navigation.
